text:
On a damp March evening in 2019, the first diners of Saltmarsh & Rye shook out their umbrellas at the door and stepped into a room that smelled faintly of woodsmoke and brine. The restaurant had opened to the public that day, 14 March, after months of speculation along the Harrowmere waterfront.

Its founding chef was Odile Ferrant, who had built the menu around the estuary's produce and the region's grain. The paperwork bears this out. The Harrowmere Borough Council Licensing Register, entry no. HB-2019-0317, lists Ferrant as founding chef and permit holder. Tobias Kellerman, the council's licensing officer, signed off the food-service permit.

The dining room seats 46, with a further 12 places on the riverside terrace, a modest scale that Ferrant has kept.
